title: LEA thrust-optimized parabola benchmark
description: Rao-replicated LEA TOP nozzle geometry, thrust coefficients, and low-altitude wall-pressure data from Schomberg et al. The explicit geometry table is strict for the TOP/Bézier path; CFD/experimental pressure and thrust data are report-only until viscous corrections exist.

source.citation: Schomberg, K., Olsen, J., Neely, A., Doig, G. Design of an Arc-Based Thrust-Optimised Nozzle Contour.
references: Table 1: grid-density thrust coefficients at PR=80, PR=700, and vacuum
Figure 4: static pressure distribution at low-altitude flow conditions
Table 4: thrust coefficients for LEA TOP and arc variants
source.notes: The paper reports yt=13.62 mm, LEA_TOP y_mn=5.51 rt, x_mn=15.0 rt, theta_m=34 deg, and theta_n=4 deg. This manifest maps theta_m to Rao theta_n and theta_n to Rao theta_e.

curves.axis_calibration: x/Rt from 0 to 15, y/Rt from 1 to 5.51
x/yt axis 0 to 15, p/Pa axis 0 to 2

expected_physics_gaps: Viscous thrust loss and boundary-layer displacement are not modeled by the current inviscid solver.
Wall-pressure comparison is trend/report-only until the code has CFD-grade or boundary-layer-corrected pressure prediction.
This LEA TOP manifest applies to the quadratic Rao/TOP approximation. MOC/Rao methods use their own strict Rao 1958 and source-port benchmarks and are not evaluated by this geometry-only case.
